title: Grateful Dead Live at Music Hall on 1972-10-26
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude Professional v7.02 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crisp sound‑board capture of a soaring second set – epic Playing in the Band, fiery Deal and powerful Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller remaster delivers a clean, well‑balanced mix that lets every instrument shine, though a faint hiss and an over‑present bass drum are noted. Musically the show shines on the second half with a monster “Playing in the Band” opener, a soaring “Deal”, and a tight “Bird Song”/“Dark Star” run, while the first set is considered solid but not earth‑shaking.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate 4–5 stars and praise both performance and sound; detailed comments on mix, song highlights and band playing give a reliable consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix described as perfect, crisp and clean; occasional hiss in early sections and an overly prominent bass drum noted by some listeners.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set solid but unremarkable; second set launches with a blistering “Playing in the Band” and maintains high intensity through Deal, Dark Star and Sugar Magnolia.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for cosmic guitar tone, razor‑sharp riffs and soaring solos throughout the night.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as brilliant on many jams but was not properly miked on this recording, reducing his presence; still “bombs” when audible.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal flubs and weaker singing cited, especially toward the show’s end.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano and Rhodes work highlighted, with interesting pedal effects adding texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is more audible than usual; Mickey Hart’s bass drum is described as overly prominent and sometimes obtrusive.
